headline: Ready for school, in her own way

before_slider.lead: Isenathi is almost five. With her family and Siyakwazi beside her, she has gone from learning to sit to starting preschool.

before_slider.p: She lives with cerebral palsy. When Siyakwazi's therapists began working with her, they started with the basics: sitting, then crawling. Very quickly she was pulling herself up to stand, then walking with a little trolley. Soon she didn't need the trolley at all.

before_slider.quote: "Her gross motor skills were the quickest to develop," says her therapist.
"But the biggest change in Isenathi is her social communication. She's so bubbly and bright, talks so beautifully, and engages with people."

after_slider.p: That didn't happen by accident. Her mom took part from the very beginning, with her uncle and her gogo (grandmother) alongside. Her mom joined Siyakwazi's parent support group. Her uncle joined the Siyakwazi sewing hub, where he makes learning resources for other children and earns an income for the household. At home, her mom and gogo made sure she knew her body parts and basic concepts, a strong foundation for school.
This year Isenathi started preschool, where her teachers give her the extra support she needs in the classroom.

after_slider.display: One child. A whole family lifted.

after_slider.p: Siyakwazi's work goes beyond therapy. It supports parents, creates income for families, and helps preschools welcome children with disabilities. In 2025, it supported 170 children with disabilities and their families. Gifts to Even Ground help fund community-led programs like this one, so more children like Isenathi can start school ready to learn.
